1	# Mobile View — plan
2	
3	A mobile-friendly copy of the sheet lives in **`Character Sheet (Mobile).html`**.
4	It is a byte-for-byte copy of `Character Sheet.html` plus two small, clearly
5	fenced additions. We iterate on it here, then fold it back into the main sheet
6	as a built-in **Mobile View** once it feels right.
7	
8	## What the copy changes (and only this)
9	
10	The copy keeps the same single-file, no-build, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS philosophy.
11	Three minimal diffs from the original:
12	
13	1. **`<title>`** — `Character Sheet · Mobile` (so you can tell the open file
14	   apart). Cosmetic.
15	2. **A `MOBILE VIEW` `@media (max-width:820px)` block** appended at the end of
16	   the `<style>`. Width-gated, so on a laptop the sheet renders exactly like the
17	   desktop original — nothing in the block applies above 820px.
18	3. **A small `MOBILE VIEW enhancement` `<script>`** just before `</body>`. It
19	   *adds* a second `#pagetabs` click listener (it does not replace the existing
20	   one), so on a narrow screen tapping a tab centres it in the swipeable tab bar
21	   and scrolls back to the top of the page.
22	
23	Both code additions are wrapped in `MOBILE VIEW` banner comments so they are
24	trivial to locate and lift out.
25	
26	### What the mobile block does
27	
28	- **No zoom-on-focus** — pins `input/select/textarea` to `font-size:16px` (iOS
29	  zooms a focused field smaller than that).
30	- **Toolbar** goes static and compact; the brand takes its own row and the
31	  action buttons grow to ≥42px tall touch targets.
32	- **Page tabs** become a single **pinned, horizontally-swipeable row** (the 9+
33	  tabs no longer wrap). The tab bar owns the sticky top spot instead of the
34	  toolbar.
35	- **Header** stacks the portrait centered above the identity fields.
36	- **Two-column regions** (`.columns`, `.topblock`) stack to one column at 820px
37	  (the originals only collapsed at 860/640).
38	- **Bigger touch targets** for skill/save checkboxes and ability steppers.
39	- **Modals** (Create Character wizard, Settings) go near full-screen with a
40	  sticky header/footer and an internal scroll.
41	- **Settings** section nav stays a scrollable row.
42	
43	Everything is additive CSS/JS — no existing rule, id, data model, autosave key,
44	or computation is touched, so a character saved in one file opens in the other.
45	
46	## How to fold it into the main sheet (later)
47	
48	Goal: one file, `Character Sheet.html`, that is responsive by width **and** has
49	an explicit, user-toggleable Mobile View.
50	
51	1. **Copy the two fenced blocks** (the `MOBILE VIEW` `@media` block and the
52	   `MOBILE VIEW enhancement` `<script>`) into `Character Sheet.html`. Because the
53	   `@media` block is width-gated and the script is additive, this alone makes the
54	   main sheet responsive with zero risk to desktop rendering. This is the safe
55	   first merge.
56	2. **Add a manual toggle** (so it can be forced on a desktop/tablet, and
57	   remembered): add a **"Mobile view"** switch under **Settings → Layout/General**.
58	   The toggle adds/removes a `mobile` class on `<html>` (or `.sheet`) and persists
59	   it in the same per-browser settings store the other layout toggles use
60	   (`hiddenPages`, `hidePortrait`, …).
61	3. **Make the mobile rules fire on the class too**, not just the width. Change
62	   the block's guard from `@media (max-width:820px){ … }` to a shared selector,
63	   e.g. duplicate the gate:
64	   ```css
65	   @media (max-width:820px){ /* …rules… */ }
66	   html.mobile .toolbar, html.mobile .pagetabs, /* …mirror the same rules… */
67	   ```
68	   In practice the cleanest port is to drop the `@media` and instead scope every
69	   rule under `html.mobile`, then have the toggle default to *on* below 820px via

# Browser Render (flash-free HTML → image)

When you need to render a local HTML/SVG file to a PNG or PDF to inspect it (e.g. checking how a generated page, character sheet, or report looks), do NOT launch Chrome with `--headless=new`. On macOS that mode spins up a real GPU/window surface and produces a visible **white screen flash** on every launch. In a tight render→check→fix loop that strobes the whole display every few seconds and reads, to the user, like something is repeatedly taking a screenshot. (This was the cause of a real "my screen keeps flashing" report on 2026-06-03 — a render loop on the D&D character sheet.)

Important: the flash is purely cosmetic — headless Chrome screenshots a **file**, never the user's actual screen, so there is no privacy/capture concern. But it is alarming and unnecessary. Use a flash-free path.

## Preferred: `--headless=old`

One-flag change. The legacy headless mode renders fully offscreen (no window surface, no flash):

```bash
CHROME="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
"$CHROME" --headless=old --disable-gpu --no-first-run \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/render-$$ --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=1000,1400 --screenshot=/tmp/out.png \
  "file:///tmp/page.html"
```

Verified to still produce a PNG on Chrome 148 (2026-06-03), even though old headless was nominally removed around Chrome 132 — the flag is still honored. **Caveat:** confirmed it *renders*; the no-flash behavior was not visually self-verified (can't see the screen from a tool). If you switch a loop to `--headless=old` and the user still reports flashing, Chrome is likely aliasing `old`→`new` on their version — fall back to Playwright below.

## Robust fallback: Playwright (best for JS-heavy pages)

If `--headless=old` still flashes, or the page needs real JS execution / interaction (clicking tabs, waiting on load), use Playwright's true-headless Chromium — it does not create an on-screen window on macOS:

```bash
# one-time: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
python3 - <<'PY'
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()                 # headless by default, no flash
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width":1000,"height":1400})
    pg.goto("file:///tmp/page.html")
    pg.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
    # pg.click('.ptab[data-page="spells"]')  # real interaction if needed
    pg.screenshot(path="/tmp/out.png", full_page=True)
    b.close()
PY
```

## Other options (static HTML only, no JS)

- `qlmanage -t -s 1400 -o /tmp "/tmp/page.html"` — macOS Quick Look, native, no flash, but ignores most JS.
- `wkhtmltoimage page.html out.png` — old WebKit, offscreen, no flash; weak JS. (`brew install --cask wkhtmltopdf`)

## Cleanup

Each Chrome render leaves a throwaway `--user-data-dir` and PNG in `/tmp`. Use a unique dir per call (e.g. `/tmp/render-$$`) and sweep stale ones afterward:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/render-* /tmp/cs* /tmp/cnd*   # stale headless profiles
```

## Rule of thumb

Default to `--headless=old`. Reach for Playwright when the page is JS-driven or the flash persists. Never leave a raw `--headless=new` in a loop that runs while the user is at the machine.

## What I changed (one file: `Character Sheet.html`)
1. **Mobile CSS block** — lifted the mobile sheet's `@media (max-width:820px)` rules, but rescoped every rule under `html.mobile` instead of a width query. That's what lets the toggle force it on at *any* width.
2. **Toolbar "Mobile" button** (+ a floating Save that only appears in mobile view, since the static toolbar scrolls off-screen there).
3. **A small self-contained script** that toggles `html.mobile`, remembers your choice in `localStorage` per browser, and auto-enables below 820px when you haven't set a preference. Also ported the tab-centering behavior (tap a tab → it centers in the swipe bar and jumps to top).

## Per your two choices
- **Mobile layout only** — desktop renders exactly as before. I deliberately left out the mobile file's non-layout extras (flat/square corners globally, tab content-dots, the backup-reminder banner, numeric-keypad hints). Note: square corners *do* apply inside the mobile view itself, but never to desktop.
- **Auto + button** — on automatically on phones, plus the manual toggle, remembered per browser.

**No character data touched** — the toggle only adds/removes a CSS class and writes one cosmetic `localStorage` key (`dnd_sheet_mobileview`); a character saved before still loads identically.

## Two follow-ups I did *not* do (your call)
- **The standalone files are now redundant.** `Character Sheet (Mobile).html` and `MOBILE-VIEW-PLAN.md` exist only because the mobile work lived separately. The plan itself says to delete them once folded in and verified — but I didn't, since I didn't create them. Want me to remove them (or keep the plan as a README roadmap note)?
- **Not committed.** The repo (`BaesTheorem/dnd-character-sheet`) has uncommitted changes. Say the word and I'll commit/push.

One caveat on the extras you declined: the numeric-keypad hint has zero desktop effect and only helps typing numbers on a phone — easy to add later if you want it, but I left it out to honor "mobile layout only."

blocks.text:
The core constraint here is worth stating plainly, because it shapes everything: **to open on an iPhone with no app *and* reliably remember a character between sessions, the file needs to live at a web URL opened in Safari.** iOS can open an HTML file you AirDrop/email, but it opens in a sandboxed preview that doesn't reliably persist `localStorage` — so changes (HP, spell slots, notes) get lost. The robust path is a hosted link + Safari's **"Add to Home Screen"** (which makes an app-like icon with no App Store install — that satisfies "no extra apps").

The one wrinkle is your project's rule about never exposing the copyrighted PHB data publicly. How I solve that depends on two things only you can answer:

blocks.name: AskUserQuestion

questions.question: What do your players actually need to do on their phones?

options.label: View + track a character I build
options.description: You (DM) build each character on your Mac with full PHB data, then hand it off. On their phone they just view it and track play (HP, spell slots used, notes, checkboxes). This needs NO copyrighted data on their phone — cleanest legally.

options.label: Build their own from scratch
options.description: Players use the Create Character wizard, spell pickers, item lists themselves on their phone. This requires sourcebook data to reach their phone, which forces a choice between SRD-only (legal) or full PHB (copyright gray area).

questions.question: How do you want to get the sheet onto their phones?

options.label: GitHub Pages link
options.description: Free hosting on your existing public repo. Players open one link in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → app-like icon that saves offline. Recommended — most convenient and persists data. I'd add iOS web-app meta tags + an icon.

options.label: Send each player a file
options.description: AirDrop/email/iMessage a self-contained HTML file. Zero hosting setup, but on iPhone it opens in a preview that does NOT reliably save changes between sessions. Fine for a one-time view, poor for ongoing play.

options.label: Private/unlisted host
options.description: Host the full-PHB version at an unguessable URL (Cloudflare/Netlify). All features work, persists via Add to Home Screen, but puts copyrighted data on a web URL — against this repo's no-copyrighted-data rule. Your call.

## The one caveat I have to be straight about
This is the limitation I flagged before, and it still applies to the file-send route. The app keeps your character two ways:
- **Auto-save** to the browser's local storage (per origin), and
- **Save** → downloads a *new* HTML file with your character baked in (this is the app's durable, file-based backup, designed for moving between devices).

When a file is opened from **Files** on iOS, it runs in a preview sandbox where **local storage isn't guaranteed to survive closing and reopening**, and a programmatic download (the **Save** button) may be blocked. I can't test real iOS hardware from here, so before you rely on it for a campaign, have one player do this 60-second check on an actual iPhone:

> Open the file → type a name in **Character name** → tap **Save** (does a new `.html` download to Files?) → fully close → reopen the *original* file (did the name persist?).

- If **Save** works → the durable workflow is: edit → **Save** → reopen the saved file next session. Solid.
- If **neither** persists → the file is fine for a one-session view but won't remember changes, and the **hosted-link + Add to Home Screen** route is the only bulletproof fix (I can still set that up — your private/unlisted-host idea, or the SRD-legal public version).
